skill.name: remotion-maps
skill.description: Build deterministic 2D and 3D map animations in Remotion using static images, Mapbox, MapLibre, MapTiler, or CesiumJS.
skill.summary: Choose and implement a stable Remotion map technique for each animated shot.
skill.author: remotion-dev

security_audit.summary: The review confirmed one medium supply-chain risk because the Cesium component executes a remote script without integrity verification. Other static alerts are false positives caused by templates, documentation, fixed paths, named provider tokens, and local frame capture. Separate guidance to use unrestricted MapTiler keys creates a high-confidence credential-abuse risk.

remediation.issue: The instructions recommend an unrestricted MapTiler key.
remediation.suggestion: Use a dedicated key with provider-supported restrictions, strict quotas, and monitoring. Remove all guidance that recommends unrestricted credentials.

remediation.issue: CesiumJS is dynamically loaded from a remote CDN without integrity verification.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle a pinned Cesium package or vendor audited assets locally. Otherwise, add integrity verification and an explicit trusted-source policy.

content.value_statement: Animated maps often shimmer, load late, or use unsuitable geographic sources. This skill guides deterministic Remotion implementations across static, 2D, annotated, and 3D map techniques.
actual_capabilities: Selects among static images, Mapbox, MapLibre, MapTiler, and CesiumJS for a specific Remotion shot.
Provides frame-driven patterns for routes, labels, borders, camera movement, and 3D flythroughs.
Uses Remotion render gates to wait for map tiles, WebGL scenes, and per-frame updates.
Explains fixed map plates that reduce shimmer during moving 2D camera effects.
Includes local scripts for preparing route paths, country metadata, borders, and Cesium camera paths.
limitations: The examples require an existing Remotion project and the relevant map libraries.
Most interactive map techniques require network access, and several require provider credentials.
Live 2D camera motion can shimmer during headless rendering, so fixed plates may be necessary.
Users must verify provider terms, attribution, geography, credential controls, and render limits.

use_cases.title: Build a Route Video
use_cases.description: Create a stable animated route with map layers, labels, and frame-based progress.

use_cases.title: Explain Geographic Evidence
use_cases.description: Combine provider tiles with verified GeoJSON for rivers, borders, and country-entry timing.

use_cases.title: Produce a 3D Flyover
use_cases.description: Plan a Cesium terrain or city flight with smooth paths and deterministic frame capture.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Static Locator
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Remotion locator shot for [place]. Use one static image at [dimensions]. Add fixed labels for [locations] and preserve attribution.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a MapLibre Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a [duration]-second MapLibre route from [start] to [end]. Draw the route by frame and keep the map deterministic during rendering.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Geography with MapTiler
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a MapTiler explainer for [topic]. Compare provider vector data with supplied GeoJSON. Animate [features] and document each geographic source.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Cesium Flythrough
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Cesium [landscape or city] flythrough along [path]. Smooth camera motion, restrict provider keys, preserve attribution, and verify representative rendered frames.

output_examples.input: Create a ten-second route animation from Zurich to New York without a paid map key.
output_examples.output: A MapLibre implementation plan using a great-circle route, a fixed map plate, frame-based line progress, and provider attribution.

output_examples.input: Show a river entering three countries, with each border and label appearing at the correct time.
output_examples.output: A MapTiler workflow that prepares ordered GeoJSON, calculates country-entry stops, and synchronizes river, border, fill, and label animations.

output_examples.input: Create a cinematic flight through a mountain gorge for a 20-second Remotion composition.
output_examples.output: A Cesium landscape plan with a smoothed camera path, MapTiler terrain, fixed altitude controls, render gates, and representative frame checks.

best_practices: Choose one map technique for each shot and load only its relevant guidance.
Drive every animation from the Remotion frame and wait for map resources before capture.
Use dedicated restricted provider keys, preserve attribution, and record geographic sources.
anti_patterns: Do not move a live 2D map camera every frame before testing a rendered clip.
Do not hand-build geodesic calculations when Turf already provides the required operation.
Do not use unrestricted production credentials or remove required provider attribution.

faq.question: Which map technique should I choose?
faq.answer: Use a static image for fixed context, MapLibre for free 2D maps, MapTiler for annotations, and CesiumJS for 3D flyovers.

faq.question: Do all techniques require an API key?
faq.answer: No. Static images and MapLibre can work without a key. Mapbox, MapTiler, and the listed Cesium provider modes require credentials.

faq.question: How does the skill improve render stability?
faq.answer: It uses frame-driven updates, render gates, disabled interactions, fixed map plates, and checks of rendered output.

faq.question: Can it animate custom geographic data?
faq.answer: Yes. The MapTiler guidance combines provider layers with custom GeoJSON and includes scripts for ordered routes, borders, and label metadata.

faq.question: Does it support genuine 3D camera movement?
faq.answer: CesiumJS supports terrain and city flythroughs. The 2D Mapbox, MapLibre, and MapTiler techniques do not provide genuine changing 3D cameras.

faq.question: What must I verify before publishing a video?
faq.answer: Verify rendered pixels, provider attribution, usage terms, credential restrictions, geographic sources, and every required aspect ratio.
